title: Where to eat on a first weekend in New York
variant: Places: twelve pins over the city, a card grouped by time of day, photos
prompt: I'm in New York for the first time next weekend. Where should I eat? Put it on a map so I can see what's near what.
note: The places shape, and the one that shows the list-is-the-data rule at full size: twelve entries carry their own coordinates and the script draws pins from them, so the page has one copy of every name and position. The card is grouped by the time of day a first visit would use each place, which does the legend's work without a legend; the pins are one color and one shape because every place here is the same kind of thing. Each entry carries a real photo of the place from Wikimedia Commons, cropped to 3:2 at 480 wide, and the popup clones the entry's image rather than carrying a second copy, so twelve photos cost half a megabyte rather than one. Under each entry are the two links out, the place's own site and a Google Maps search for its name and street, kept small so neither reads as the click that goes to the pin. Ten of the twelve fall between Union Square and Canal Street and the first frame shows that beside the card; the two in Brooklyn are their own group so the reader knows they are a train ride. Positions came from Nominatim and the folded sources say so; what to order is called shorthand rather than research, and hours and prices are not stated.
